import Mathlib.RingTheory.Polynomial.Basic
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Ideal.Maps
import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.PNat.Basic
import Mathlib.RingTheory.PrincipalIdealDomain

/-!
# Finite polynomial descriptions of stabilisers

The finite-generation step of Acuaviva--Kania, Lemma 2.1(ii), is a consequence
of the Hilbert basis theorem. We prove that an arbitrary family of polynomial
equations in finitely many variables has the same zero locus as a finite
subfamily of the original equations. For equations grouped by tensor degree,
finitely many whole degrees already suffice.

This module does not assume that moment constraints are polynomial: their
concrete polynomial encoding and their characterisation of the body stabiliser
are separate statements. No compactness, symmetry or convexity is used here.
-/

namespace BanachIsometric

/-- In a Noetherian ring the ideal generated by an arbitrary set is already
generated by a finite subset of that same set. -/
theorem exists_finset_same_ideal_span {A : Type*} [CommSemiring A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (S : Set A) :
    ∃ T : Finset A, (T : Set A) ⊆ S ∧ Ideal.span S = Ideal.span (T : Set A) := by
  exact (Submodule.fg_span_iff_fg_span_finset_subset S).mp
    (IsNoetherian.noetherian (Submodule.span A S))

/-- The common zero locus of any polynomial equations in finitely many
variables is cut out by finitely many of the original equations. -/
theorem exists_finset_same_polynomial_zeros
    {σ R : Type*} [Finite σ] [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (S : Set (MvPolynomial σ R)) :
    ∃ T : Finset (MvPolynomial σ R), (T : Set (MvPolynomial σ R)) ⊆ S ∧
      ∀ x : σ → R,
        (∀ P ∈ S, MvPolynomial.eval x P = 0) ↔
          ∀ P ∈ T, MvPolynomial.eval x P = 0 := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨T, hTS, hspan⟩ := exists_finset_same_ideal_span S
  refine ⟨T, hTS, ?_⟩
  intro x
  constructor
  · intro h P hP
    exact h P (hTS hP)
  · intro h P hP
    have hker : Ideal.span (T : Set (MvPolynomial σ R)) ≤
        RingHom.ker (MvPolynomial.eval x) := by
      rw [Ideal.span_le]
      intro Q hQ
      exact RingHom.mem_ker.mpr (h Q hQ)
    exact RingHom.mem_ker.mp (hker (by
      rw [← hspan]
      exact Ideal.subset_span hP))

/-- The finite equations may be selected by their original indices; repeated
polynomials or an infinite index set cause no difficulty. -/
theorem exists_finset_same_indexed_polynomial_zeros
    {σ R ι : Type*} [Finite σ] [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (P : ι → MvPolynomial σ R) :
    ∃ I : Finset ι, ∀ x : σ → R,
      (∀ i, MvPolynomial.eval x (P i) = 0) ↔
        ∀ i ∈ I, MvPolynomial.eval x (P i) = 0 := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨T, hT, hzero⟩ := exists_finset_same_polynomial_zeros (Set.range P)
  have himage : (T : Set (MvPolynomial σ R)) ⊆ P '' Set.univ := by
    simpa using hT
  obtain ⟨I, _, hI⟩ := Finset.subset_set_image_iff.mp himage
  refine ⟨I, ?_⟩
  intro x
  constructor
  · intro h i _
    exact h i
  · intro h i
    apply (hzero x).mpr ?_ (P i) (Set.mem_range_self i)
    intro Q hQ
    rw [← hI] at hQ
    obtain ⟨j, hj, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hQ
    exact h j hj

/-- Suppose constraints are grouped into blocks (for example, tensor degrees
and their components). There are finitely many blocks whose full constraints
already imply every constraint in the entire family. No finiteness assumption
on the set of components in any one block is needed. -/
theorem exists_finset_same_polynomial_blocks
    {σ R ι : Type*} [Finite σ] [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    {κ : ι → Type*} (P : ∀ i, κ i → MvPolynomial σ R) :
    ∃ I : Finset ι, ∀ x : σ → R,
      (∀ i j, MvPolynomial.eval x (P i j) = 0) ↔
        ∀ i ∈ I, ∀ j, MvPolynomial.eval x (P i j) = 0 := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨T, hT⟩ := exists_finset_same_indexed_polynomial_zeros
    (fun ij : Sigma κ => P ij.1 ij.2)
  refine ⟨T.image Sigma.fst, ?_⟩
  intro x
  constructor
  · intro h i _ j
    exact h i j
  · intro h i j
    apply (hT x).mpr ?_ ⟨i, j⟩
    intro ij hij
    exact h ij.1 (Finset.mem_image_of_mem Sigma.fst hij) ij.2

/-- Polynomial equality constraints have the same finite-block property.
Taking positive integers for `ι` selects finitely many positive tensor degrees. -/
theorem exists_finset_same_polynomial_equality_blocks
    {σ R ι : Type*} [Finite σ] [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    {κ : ι → Type*} (P Q : ∀ i, κ i → MvPolynomial σ R) :
    ∃ I : Finset ι, ∀ x : σ → R,
      (∀ i j, MvPolynomial.eval x (P i j) = MvPolynomial.eval x (Q i j)) ↔
        ∀ i ∈ I, ∀ j,
          MvPolynomial.eval x (P i j) = MvPolynomial.eval x (Q i j) := by
  obtain ⟨I, hI⟩ := exists_finset_same_polynomial_blocks
    (fun i j => P i j - Q i j)
  refine ⟨I, ?_⟩
  intro x
  simpa only [map_sub, sub_eq_zero] using hI x

/-!
For the application to moments we work directly with full tensor-coordinate
arrays. If `A` is the matrix of a real linear map and `M` is a degree-`r` array,
the transformed entry is the sum over input coordinates of `M` times one
matrix entry for each tensor slot. Symmetry of `M` is unnecessary for the
finite-generation argument.
-/

/-- The polynomial giving one coordinate of the `r`-fold tensor action. -/
noncomputable def tensorEntryPolynomial (m r : ℕ)
    (M : (Fin r → Fin m) → ℝ) (out : Fin r → Fin m) :
    MvPolynomial (Fin m × Fin m) ℝ :=
  ∑ inp : Fin r → Fin m,
    MvPolynomial.C (M inp) * ∏ k : Fin r, MvPolynomial.X (out k, inp k)

/-- The usual coordinate formula for the tensor power of a matrix. -/
noncomputable def tensorCoordinateAction {m r : ℕ} (A : Fin m → Fin m → ℝ)
    (M : (Fin r → Fin m) → ℝ) (out : Fin r → Fin m) : ℝ :=
  ∑ inp : Fin r → Fin m, M inp * ∏ k : Fin r, A (out k) (inp k)

/-- Evaluation proves that the tensor-coordinate action is polynomial in the
entries of the transforming matrix. -/
theorem tensorEntryPolynomial_eval {m r : ℕ} (A : Fin m → Fin m → ℝ)
    (M : (Fin r → Fin m) → ℝ) (out : Fin r → Fin m) :
    MvPolynomial.eval (fun ij : Fin m × Fin m => A ij.1 ij.2)
      (tensorEntryPolynomial m r M out) = tensorCoordinateAction A M out := by
  simp [tensorEntryPolynomial, tensorCoordinateAction]

/-- On a pure tensor the coordinate action applies the matrix independently
in every slot. This checks the coordinate formula against the tensor-power
action rather than merely assigning that name to an arbitrary polynomial. -/
theorem tensorCoordinateAction_pure {m r : ℕ} (A : Fin m → Fin m → ℝ)
    (v : Fin r → Fin m → ℝ) (out : Fin r → Fin m) :
    tensorCoordinateAction A (fun inp => ∏ k : Fin r, v k (inp k)) out =
      ∏ k : Fin r, ∑ j : Fin m, A (out k) j * v k j := by
  unfold tensorCoordinateAction
  calc
    (∑ inp : Fin r → Fin m,
        (∏ k : Fin r, v k (inp k)) * ∏ k : Fin r, A (out k) (inp k)) =
        ∑ inp : Fin r → Fin m, ∏ k : Fin r, A (out k) (inp k) * v k (inp k) := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro inp _
      rw [← Finset.prod_mul_distrib]
      apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
      intro k _
      exact mul_comm _ _
    _ = ∏ k : Fin r, ∑ j : Fin m, A (out k) j * v k j := by
      simpa using
        (Finset.prod_univ_sum (fun _ : Fin r => (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m)))
          (fun k j => A (out k) j * v k j)).symm

/-- For any full sequence of real tensors of positive degrees, the common
matrix stabiliser is already the stabiliser of finitely many selected degrees.
In particular this applies to the moment tensors in Lemma 2.1(ii), once their
coordinate transformation rule is established. No evenness or symmetry of the
arrays is required, so odd moments are retained. -/
theorem exists_finset_tensor_stabilizer_degrees (m : ℕ)
    (M : (d : ℕ+) → (Fin (d : ℕ) → Fin m) → ℝ) :
    ∃ I : Finset ℕ+, ∀ A : Fin m → Fin m → ℝ,
      (∀ d, tensorCoordinateAction A (M d) = M d) ↔
        ∀ d ∈ I, tensorCoordinateAction A (M d) = M d := by
  obtain ⟨I, hI⟩ := exists_finset_same_polynomial_equality_blocks
    (fun d : ℕ+ => fun out : Fin (d : ℕ) → Fin m =>
      tensorEntryPolynomial m (d : ℕ) (M d) out)
    (fun d : ℕ+ => fun out : Fin (d : ℕ) → Fin m =>
      MvPolynomial.C (M d out))
  refine ⟨I, ?_⟩
  intro A
  simpa only [tensorEntryPolynomial_eval, MvPolynomial.eval_C, funext_iff] using
    hI (fun ij : Fin m × Fin m => A ij.1 ij.2)

/-- Equivalently, moments through some finite positive degree suffice.
This cumulative version is convenient when moments are handled successively. -/
theorem exists_tensor_stabilizer_degree_bound (m : ℕ)
    (M : (d : ℕ+) → (Fin (d : ℕ) → Fin m) → ℝ) :
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ A : Fin m → Fin m → ℝ,
      (∀ d, tensorCoordinateAction A (M d) = M d) ↔
        ∀ d : ℕ+, (d : ℕ) ≤ N → tensorCoordinateAction A (M d) = M d := by
  obtain ⟨I, hI⟩ := exists_finset_tensor_stabilizer_degrees m M
  refine ⟨I.sup (fun d : ℕ+ => (d : ℕ)), ?_⟩
  intro A
  constructor
  · intro h d _
    exact h d
  · intro h
    apply (hI A).mpr
    intro d hd
    exact h d (Finset.le_sup hd)

end BanachIsometric

  ∑ inp : Fin r → Fin m, M inp * ∏ k : Fin r, A (out k) (inp k)
declarations.doc: The usual coordinate formula for the tensor power of a matrix.

/-!
# Finite polynomial descriptions of stabilisers

The finite-generation step of Acuaviva--Kania, Lemma 2.1(ii), is a consequence
of the Hilbert basis theorem. We prove that an arbitrary family of polynomial
equations in finitely many variables has the same zero locus as a finite
subfamily of the original equations. For equations grouped by tensor degree,
finitely many whole degrees already suffice.

This module does not assume that moment constraints are polynomial: their
concrete polynomial encoding and their characterisation of the body stabiliser
are separate statements. No compactness, symmetry or convexity is used here.
-/

namespace BanachIsometric

theorem tensorEntryPolynomial_eval {m r : ℕ} (A : Fin m → Fin m → ℝ)
    (M : (Fin r → Fin m) → ℝ) (out : Fin r → Fin m) :
    MvPolynomial.eval (fun ij : Fin m × Fin m => A ij.1 ij.2)
      (tensorEntryPolynomial m r M out) = tensorCoordinateAction A M out := by
  simp [tensorEntryPolynomial, tensorCoordinateAction]

declarations.name: tensorCoordinateAction_pure
declarations.label: tensorCoordinateAction_pure
declarations.code:
theorem tensorCoordinateAction_pure {m r : ℕ} (A : Fin m → Fin m → ℝ)
    (v : Fin r → Fin m → ℝ) (out : Fin r → Fin m) :
    tensorCoordinateAction A (fun inp => ∏ k : Fin r, v k (inp k)) out =
      ∏ k : Fin r, ∑ j : Fin m, A (out k) j * v k j := by
  unfold tensorCoordinateAction
  calc
    (∑ inp : Fin r → Fin m,
        (∏ k : Fin r, v k (inp k)) * ∏ k : Fin r, A (out k) (inp k)) =
        ∑ inp : Fin r → Fin m, ∏ k : Fin r, A (out k) (inp k) * v k (inp k) := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro inp _
      rw [← Finset.prod_mul_distrib]
      apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
      intro k _
      exact mul_comm _ _
    _ = ∏ k : Fin r, ∑ j : Fin m, A (out k) j * v k j := by
      simpa using
        (Finset.prod_univ_sum (fun _ : Fin r => (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m)))
          (fun k j => A (out k) j * v k j)).symm
declarations.signature:
theorem tensorCoordinateAction_pure {m r : ℕ} (A : Fin m → Fin m → ℝ)
    (v : Fin r → Fin m → ℝ) (out : Fin r → Fin m) :
    tensorCoordinateAction A (fun inp => ∏ k : Fin r, v k (inp k)) out =
      ∏ k : Fin r, ∑ j : Fin m, A (out k) j * v k j
declarations.doc:
On a pure tensor the coordinate action applies the matrix independently
in every slot. This checks the coordinate formula against the tensor-power
action rather than merely assigning that name to an arbitrary polynomial.

declarations.name: exists_finset_tensor_stabilizer_degrees
declarations.label: exists_finset_tensor_stabilizer_degrees
declarations.code:
theorem exists_finset_tensor_stabilizer_degrees (m : ℕ)
    (M : (d : ℕ+) → (Fin (d : ℕ) → Fin m) → ℝ) :
    ∃ I : Finset ℕ+, ∀ A : Fin m → Fin m → ℝ,
      (∀ d, tensorCoordinateAction A (M d) = M d) ↔
        ∀ d ∈ I, tensorCoordinateAction A (M d) = M d := by
  obtain ⟨I, hI⟩ := exists_finset_same_polynomial_equality_blocks
    (fun d : ℕ+ => fun out : Fin (d : ℕ) → Fin m =>
      tensorEntryPolynomial m (d : ℕ) (M d) out)
    (fun d : ℕ+ => fun out : Fin (d : ℕ) → Fin m =>
      MvPolynomial.C (M d out))
  refine ⟨I, ?_⟩
  intro A
  simpa only [tensorEntryPolynomial_eval, MvPolynomial.eval_C, funext_iff] using
    hI (fun ij : Fin m × Fin m => A ij.1 ij.2)

    (M : (d : ℕ+) → (Fin (d : ℕ) → Fin m) → ℝ) :
    ∃ I : Finset ℕ+, ∀ A : Fin m → Fin m → ℝ,
      (∀ d, tensorCoordinateAction A (M d) = M d) ↔
        ∀ d ∈ I, tensorCoordinateAction A (M d) = M d
declarations.doc:
For any full sequence of real tensors of positive degrees, the common
matrix stabiliser is already the stabiliser of finitely many selected degrees.
In particular this applies to the moment tensors in Lemma 2.1(ii), once their
coordinate transformation rule is established. No evenness or symmetry of the
arrays is required, so odd moments are retained.

declarations.name: exists_tensor_stabilizer_degree_bound
declarations.label: exists_tensor_stabilizer_degree_bound
declarations.code:
theorem exists_tensor_stabilizer_degree_bound (m : ℕ)
    (M : (d : ℕ+) → (Fin (d : ℕ) → Fin m) → ℝ) :
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ A : Fin m → Fin m → ℝ,
      (∀ d, tensorCoordinateAction A (M d) = M d) ↔
        ∀ d : ℕ+, (d : ℕ) ≤ N → tensorCoordinateAction A (M d) = M d := by
  obtain ⟨I, hI⟩ := exists_finset_tensor_stabilizer_degrees m M
  refine ⟨I.sup (fun d : ℕ+ => (d : ℕ)), ?_⟩
  intro A
  constructor
  · intro h d _
    exact h d
  · intro h
    apply (hI A).mpr
    intro d hd
    exact h d (Finset.le_sup hd)
